messages:
maria_r: heads up, bring-up for harbor-embed-14B on the bridge-v1 audit shows a strange nearest-neighbor drift compared to control. r@1 down, clusters fuzzier. anyone else seeing this?
liam_g: i ran a quick pass — r@1 ~ -2.8% vs control, r@5 roughly even. silhouette dropped noticeably.
alex_m: can you paste the eval command you used? want to rule out indexing/normalize ordering.
maria_r: eval command i used:
```
./eval_embeddings --model harbor-embed-14B-v1 \
  --dataset bridge-v1 --metric recall@k --k 1,5,10 \
  --knn-idx faiss_ivf --norm l2 --whiten false --threads 28
```
automated summary from run: control r@1 0.712 -> harbor 0.684 (-0.028); r@5 0.882 -> 0.876 (-0.006); silhouette 0.46 -> 0.33. mean L2 norm control 1.07, harbor 0.94. artifacts at /runs/1712345678-harbor-audit/ (vectors, faiss indices, tsne).
liam_g: interesting pattern: r@5 stable but r@1 drops = likely centroid swaps inside same label. not a complete collapse.
tara_k: do we have per-label breakdown? short queries or docs might be disproportionately affected.
maria_r: per-label heatmap in artifacts. top regressors: "news-summary", "product-descriptions". example swap:
Query: "multi-region low-latency transactional db"
control top: ["managed multi-region DB", "geo-replicated db", "serverless transactions"]
harbor top:  ["managed multi-region DB", "cloud billing guide", "backup snapshot guide"]
(leads to semantic mismatch; lexical bias to billing terms)
alex_m: hm lexical drift could be from vocab merges or new tokenizer merges in harbor. or from quant/rescaling at encode time. did you compare embedding norm distributions and per-dim variance?
maria_r: yes distribution tighter for harbor (less dynamic range). per-dim variance lower across tail dims.
liam_g: let's test a few quick experiments: (1) harbor fp16 baseline, (2) harbor q4_0 per-channel symmetric quant, (3) harbor with no on-disk faiss norm and apply normalization post-load. compare centroid diffs and top-10 swap lists.
alex_m: i'll queue fp16 + q4_0 runs now. also compute top-10 centroid-swap table for affected labels.
eval-bot: queued run 1712345678-2 (harbor-fp16), run 1712345678-3 (harbor-q4_0). ETA ~20m. artifacts will be attached when done.
tara_k: small experiment idea: try whitening fit on control and apply to harbor vectors to see if geometry aligns. cheap check before touching tokenizer.
liam_g: also check whether normalization in the eval pipeline is applied before or after faiss index creation. order can flip nearest neighbor results.
maria_r: agreed. plan: wait for fp16/q4_0 diffs, compute per-label swap lists, try post-hoc whitening+norm. if quant causes it, we add a per-model quant profile flag and fallback to fp16 for sensitive labels. will open a short PR with suggested mitigations. thanks all. :thumbsup:
